text:
alex.g: Heads-up — after the kernel-autotune rollout I pushed yesterday, we're seeing a perf regression on long-context prefill. End-to-end latency for 4k prefill is up ~18-22% on A100 pools. Anyone else observing this?

jian.k: Yep, noticed it in the weekly perf dashboard. The autotuner started picking the 'generic_gemm_fp16' path for 4k instead of the older 'tiled_matmul_64x64_qk' kernel. Looks like the selector logic favors lower memory peak but worse throughput at long seq lengths.

maria.s: That matches my local traces. Sequence-length bucketing boundaries are "short<=512, mid<=2048, long>2048" in prod config. Prefill code path consults the bucketing heuristic to pick kernels, but decode path uses a different heuristic (per-step latency focused). We probably changed the autotune scoring to prioritize mem footprint which tipped the selector for prefill.

alex.g: Can someone paste a quick flame/trace snippet? Curious if KV cache behavior is interacting (evictions or re-allocs) during the long prefill.

devon.p: Pasting a trimmed perf snippet from a 4k prefill run (from perf-bot):

```
prefill_total: 1420 ms
  embedding/kernels:
    tiled_matmul_64x64_qk: 780 ms
    kv_copy: 120 ms
    softmax_attn: 200 ms
    other: 320 ms
post-autotune (same workload):
prefill_total: 1715 ms
  embedding/kernels:
    generic_gemm_fp16: 1150 ms
    kv_copy: 130 ms
    softmax_attn: 195 ms
    other: 240 ms
```

devon.p: Note tiled kernel had better locality with long seqs; generic path seems to incur extra GEMM overhead. Also saw occasional ephemeral KV buffer reallocs at the 3.5k token mark (those add ~10-20ms spikes).

jian.k: Two hypotheses: (1) autotuner scoring change (memory-first) bumped long-seq workloads to a suboptimal kernel; (2) our sequence-length bucketing/config mapping doesn't consider prefill vs decode differences — prefill is heavy compute all-at-once so throughput-optimized kernels should be preferred, decode is single-step so low-latency kernels win.

maria.s: Agreed. We need to separate autotune profiles for prefill vs decode and for sequence-length regimes. Also add a post-autotune canary: compare throughput vs mem across representative buckets (256/1024/4096) and prefer throughput for prefill long bucket.

perf-bot: [perf-regression] job=canary-4k-autotune detected +20% latency on prefill path (A100-prod). Full trace uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/traces/2024-03-13/1710345600-canary-4k.json

alex.g: Proposed action items: 1) rollback the kernel-autotune change for long-prefill on A100 pools (quick), 2) add separate scoring weights in autotuner config: prefill: throughput_weight=0.8, mem_weight=0.2; decode: throughput_weight=0.4, mem_weight=0.6, 3) add a new seq-bucket boundary set that tunes tiles vs generic kernels (experiment with boundary at 3k not 2k), 4) instrument KV allocations to surface realloc counts per-request.

jian.k: I'll prepare a patch to the autotuner config and a small test harness that exercises 256/1024/4096 tokens with both prefill and decode paths. Will run on a canary subset.

maria.s: I'll add metrics to the KV allocator: per-request alloc/evict counts, peak-buffer-size, and track if allocator did a reallocation (bool). Also will expose kernel-choice telemetry per model-version so we can see selector decisions over time.

devon.p: If we do the rollback, we should also hotfix the autotune scoring in the repo so future rollouts don't flip inadvertently. I'll draft an ops-rollback playbook for the rollout channel.

alex.g: Sounds good. Priority = P1 for canary/regression. Keep updates here. Thanks. :thumbsup:
